## dcfb4c64c914

**Reproduced defect — canonical domain rejected by the validator.**  Generator
SHA-256 `27d98b9d019cc4a5124f05ae5314bbf0df01cd27455760abf9132d9145705ed3`.
I ran the full battery and directly evaluated `self_check` on both canonical
training inputs and the canonical test input.  All **3/3** are rejected with the
same three complaints: the objects are not left-justified at the panel boundary,
the detected panel colors are invalid, and the row-profile difference appears
empty.  The canonical Racket rule accepts the retained input and produces the
expected output.  This is a real generator/validator domain mismatch, not a
speculative rival.

Evidence: `checks/audit/dcfb4c64c914-canonical-rejection.json`,
`checks/audit/dcfb4c64c914-canonical-racket.json`, and
`checks/audit/dcfb4c64c914-battery/checks/dcfb4c64c914_before_battery_summary.json`.
The battery additionally reports five failed stages (`lint`, `selfcheck`,
`defect_lint`, `profile_floor`, `override`).  I left this audit-only target
unchanged.

## dcfb4c64c914

**Reproduced teaching ambiguity against an undeclared bottom-alignment rival.**
The audited generator SHA-256 is
`9c665258ec35ed487f525a5ad8a66434b19146776ac6d877e13d72102ec10e47`;
the selected Racket rule hash is `53fe6f709bdc`. The declared semantic gate is
green—600/600 strict inputs, 5/5 declared witnesses and rivals, 12/12 sampled
lessons, and 0/48 ambiguous rotations—but that finite rival set omits the
plausible rule “align the two object-local row profiles at the bottom, prepend
zero padding to the shorter profile, then take absolute differences.”

I exhaustively tested every held-out position in four-pair lessons for seeds
0–999 at each of easy, medium and hard: 3,000 lessons and 12,000 rotations.
That rival survives all three demonstrations and changes the held-out answer in
**2/12,000 rotations**: easy seed 219/query 0 and medium seed 297/query 0. The
retained easy case was produced by the ordinary generator, all four inputs pass
`self_check`, and therefore it is inside the documented generator domain. The
live Racket authority matches the Python mirror on all four pairs; the rival
matches demonstration indices 1, 2 and 3 but changes query 0 from a top-padded
profile difference to a bottom-padded one.

Reproducer: `checks/audit/dcfb4c64c914/bottom-alignment-reproducer.json`.
Inputs, actual Racket outputs and rival outputs are respectively
`bottom-alignment-inputs.json`, `bottom-alignment-racket.json`, and
`bottom-alignment-rival.json` in the same directory. Aggregate probing of a
second undeclared rival is in `undeclared-rivals.json`; the first probe revision
failed only because it called a nonexistent helper, and that genuine failed run
is retained in `undeclared-rivals.log`.

**Suggested repair:** add bottom alignment to `LESSON_COMPETITORS`, then make the
unequal-height schedule profiles constructively refute it under every supported
query rotation rather than relying on random numerical noncoincidence. I did not
modify this audit-only target.
